title: Soft vs Hard Pin: UX A/B Experiment Plan
content:
Purpose
---
This doc is a working plan for an A/B experiment to measure the user-facing impact of enforcing region pinning hard (strict routing + rejection/fallback) versus soft (best-effort routing + warning/fallback). We want empirical data on: friction (failed requests, error rates surface to customers), latency/cost tradeoffs, support burden, and retention metrics for opt-in customers.

High-level hypothesis
---
Hypothesis H1: Soft-pin reduces user-visible errors and support volume but increases cross-region traffic leakage and operator-side cost by ~X%.
Hypothesis H2: Hard-pin reduces compliance risk for customers with strict residency requirements but increases transient failures for edge-case routing scenarios and will increase MTTR for customers during region outages.

Primary metrics (what success looks like)
---
- User-level success rate: percentage of requests returning a 2xx generation when a customer has a region-pin set (compare cohorts).
- Customer-visible latency p50/p95 for pinned tenants.
- Cross-region traffic ratio: fraction of tokens served from non-preferred region (telemetry tags).
- Support ticket rate per 10k requests from pinned tenants (inbound tickets mentioning region/residency).
- Compliance violations flagged by legal (binary events, monthly).
- Cost delta: infra cost per 1M tokens for pinned tenants (estimate).
- Rollback signal: any influx of SEV-level incidents related to pinning enforcement.

Secondary metrics
---
- Churn of pinned customers in 30/90 days.
- Fraction of requests using fallback model variant.
- Rate of pin-change ops (how often customers change region pin during experiment).

Experiment cohorts and sampling
---
- Universe: all tenants with an active region pin and that have >100k tokens/month historically.
- Randomize at tenant-level (not request-level) to avoid cross-contamination.
- Cohort A (soft-pin) ~ 40% of sample. Behavior: attempt regional routing, allow best-effort cross-region fallback, emit a region-leakage metric when fallback occurs; surface a non-blocking warning in tenant console and logs.
- Cohort B (hard-pin) ~ 40% of sample. Behavior: strictly enforce local-only routing; if capacity unavailable, return an explicit error with code PIN_ENFORCED_CAPACITY and use a documented fallback policy (e.g., retry to local queue for N seconds then fail).
- Holdout cohort ~20% for control (no change from current baseline behavior).
- Stratify sampling to ensure representation across: enterprise vs smb, EU vs NA pins, models used (generation vs embedding-heavy tenants).

Instrumentation plan (telemetry & logs)
---
- Add tenant-level tags: experiment.arm = soft|hard|control; region_pin = eu-west1|us-central1|etc.
- Emit events: pin.enforcement.attempt, pin.enforcement.fallback, pin.enforcement.reject, pin.enforcement.retry. Include fields: tenant_id, request_id, model, requested_sequence_length_bucket.
- Add bounded telemetry counters for cross-region token counts (avoid PII). Aggregation keys: tenant_id, day, region_from, region_to, model.
- Dashboard: quick glance panels for success rate, p95 latency, cross-region leakage, and support ticket trend.
- Combine with sampled traces for 1% of failing requests to capture full routing path for SRE/debug.

Experiment runtime and rollout steps
---
- Phase 0 (now → 2025-11-17): internal dry run against synthetic tenants (QA cluster). Smoke test enforcement/rejection flows and logs.
- Phase 1 (2025-11-18 → 2026-01-05): small pilot (10 tenants, mix of enterprise and SMB) to validate instrumentation and customer messaging templates.
- Phase 2 (2026-01-06 → 2026-02-03): ramp to full experiment sample defined above. Monitor daily metrics; weekly stakeholder sync.
- Phase 3 (2026-02-04 → 2026-02-18): analysis window and decision meeting (product + legal + SRE + CS).

Guardrails and safety
---
- Auto-abort thresholds (if any threshold crossed, abort experiment and roll back affected tenants to control):
  - More than 1% absolute drop in tenant-level success rate compared to baseline for >3 consecutive days.
  - >20% increase in support tickets from pinned tenants relative to baseline week.
  - Any compliance/legal incident flagged (immediate abort).
- Soft communications: customers in soft-pin arm will receive in-console banner: "Your tenant is in soft-residency mode: we will prefer your chosen region, but may fallback if capacity is limited." Link to FAQ.
- Hard communications: we will send an email template to tenants in hard-pin cohort before experiment starts: notice of stricter enforcement and how to request temporary exceptions during outages.

Customer messaging & CS playbook (brief)
---
- Pre-run email + console banner for both arms; include expected error codes and recommended remediation steps.
- CS playbook snippet for PIN_ENFORCED_CAPACITY: check region capacity, escalate to infra team if capacity shortfall, propose temporary pin relaxation with explicit consent, log consent.
- Template escalations: include required evidence fields (tenant_id, sample request_id, timestamps, error payload).

Data privacy & compliance notes
---
- Telemetry must avoid storing full request payloads or PII. Use hashed tenant IDs and sampled request ids for trace linkage.
- Work with Legal: confirm that the soft-arm telemetry (cross-region token counters) does not violate customer contracts for customers with explicit residency SLAs.
- Record all opt-in/opt-out signals for customers to allow audit trail.

Analysis plan
---
- Pre-registered analysis scripts (R/Python notebooks in experiments repo). Primary treatment effect: difference-in-differences for success rate and latency.
- Use logistic regression for binary success with covariates: tenant size, region, baseline error rate. Report 95% CIs.
- Breakdowns: model family, sequence-length buckets, peak vs off-peak windows.
- Run a post-hoc qualitative review of sampled support tickets to surface root causes of increases.

Open questions / decisions needed
---
- Q1: fallback policy for hard-pin when local capacity is saturated. Options: (a) immediate fail with ticket to CS, (b) queue-and-retry for short window, (c) acceptance of cross-region routing after written customer consent. Need legal input.
- Q2: how to attribute cost delta to customers for billing/reporting? tie to chargeback tagging? see RES-4981.
- Q3: sampling fraction for traces — 1% might be too low to catch rare routing races. Ops input?

Action items / TODOs (owner initials)
---

- [Ethan] implement telemetry events and create Grafana panels (due 2025-11-12).
- [Maya] wire up support-runbook snippets in Zendesk macros and train CS (due 2025-11-15).
- [Carlos] implement tenant-level randomization and flags in experiment-service (PR drafted: ops#189) (due 2025-11-14).
- [Liam] prepare analysis notebook and pre-register metrics (due 2026-01-20).

Notes to self / messy thoughts
---
- We'll probably see less visible customer friction in soft-pin but theologize about long tail compliance risk. Need Legal to sign off before any customer-facing release.
- Keep experiment limited-time and fully reversible; record all changes to tenant flag state in audit log.
- Consider gating experiment for tenants with contractual residency requirements (exclude automatically).

References and useful links
---

- Related runbooks: RESIDENCY-ENFORCEMENT-RUNBOOK (see linked artifacts)
- Slack thread: #residency-experiments (link in linked_artifacts)

Appendix: sample error payloads and customer-facing wording
---
- Example error (hard-pin): {"error_code": "PIN_ENFORCED_CAPACITY", "message": "Request could not be served in pinned region due to capacity limits. Please retry or open support ticket."}
- Console banner copy (soft): "Your region preference is active — requests are routed to your region when possible. In rare cases we will fall back to ensure continuity."

End of doc — working draft.
